title: Hirelings
html:
Hirelings[1] are recruitable characters who can join and fight alongside the player. While each has a fixed body type, voice, Race, and Background, they can have their name, class, and appearance changed upon conscription from  Withers, or via the Magic Mirror any time after.

Recruitment

A hireling can be recruited by speaking to Withers at any time after reaching Level 3 and paying 100 gold. Hirelings cannot be recruited if the party is full at the time without replacing an existing party member. During recruitment, their appearance can be customised just as that of The Dark Urge and Custom origins can. However, Withers must be spoken with again to change their class and / or ability scores. Once recruited, they can immediately be instructed to stay in camp, just like any other companion. In addition to sending them to camp, they can be permanently dismissed back to the fugue plane at no cost. A hireling dismissed this way can still be re-recruited from Withers later on. If sought out again, the hireling will be at level one with its default name, class, stats and appearance; they will retain any items (equipped or not) upon return.

No more than 3 hirelings can be recruited at the same time. When not in use they always stand at the same fixed location in camp - usually near Withers. As the camp setting changes, so does their default location.

List of Hirelings

Name Race Class Background Backstory
Brinna Brightsong
 Lightfoot Halfling Bard Entertainer Brinna Brightsong's bawdy crooning was silenced by an Absolute bloodbutcher after a controversial performance in a Triel tavern.
Danton
 Mephistopheles Tiefling Druid Folk Hero Danton was a refined druid and rearer of peacocks - until he thought transforming into one would help him escape Absolutist marauders. He was wrong.
Eldra Luthrinn
 Gold Dwarf Barbarian Outlander Eldra Luthrinn, slayer of people, monsters, and cups of sweet pear tea, was shown a watery grave when hunting Absolutists in the valleys of Chionthar.
Sir Fuzzalump
 Rock Gnome Wizard Sage Sir Fuzzalump was much mocked among his playful kind for his dour demeanor and single-minded devotion to the magical investigation of cave moss. He claims not to have giggled in over a decade, and has never frolicked.
Jacelyn
 High Half-Elf Sorcerer Guild Artisan Jacelyn was born a sorcerer, the seventh son of a seventh son. The agent of the Absolute that killed him knew this, and is rumored to have remarked, 'Probably should've left it at six.'
Kerz
 Half-Orc Paladin Noble Kerz lived many years as a paladin and mercenary, years which took a hard toll on them.[2] Befriending a group of pleasant ogres, they laid down their weapon and taught a rudimentary etiquette class, before the ogres were attacked one night, and Kerz once more took up their steel.
Kree Derryck
[3] 		Duergar Warlock Charlatan Kree's penchant for killing folk with a mere whisper was prized in the Absolute's ranks, but the utter devotion to her patron was met with lethal disapproval.
Maddala Deadeye
[3] 		Human Rogue Urchin Madalla's blindness was cured by another True Soul passing through her village - so they[4] could watch it being burnt to the ground around them. Such was the price of refusing the Absolute.
Sina'zith
 Githyanki Monk Outlander Sina'zith's monastic preferences marked her a misfit among her kin - as did the illithid tadpole an Absolutist forced into her mind. For this, the githyanki slew her as an aberration.
Varanna Sunblossom
 Wood Half-Elf Fighter Soldier Once a battle-worn veteran fighting for the Absolute, Varanna learnt that loyalty to the would-be god did not protect her from the murderous whims of jealous generals.
Ver'yll Wenkiir
 Seldarine Drow Ranger Criminal Ver'yll spent his twilights scribbling odes to leafy canopies, bushels, and the merits of the noble hedgehog. When he refused to join the Absolute, its forces tore his forest and body apart.
Zenith Feur'sel
 High Elf Cleric Acolyte Zenith, once an optimistic Evereskan Graycloak, journeyed to Faerun in search of a new sunrise. An Absolute warband proved his dour father right: Zenith was doomed!

Races

Not all races and subraces are covered by hirelings, and therefore some races are only available with a custom character. Dragonborn is the only race not covered by hirelings out of the 11 playable races, and out of the 18 subraces those races have only 8 of them are covered. The races and subraces covered by hirelings are:

  •  Duergar
  •  Githyanki
  •  Gold Dwarf
  •  Half-Orc
  •  High Elf
  •  High Half-Elf
  •  Human
  •  Lightfoot Halfling
  •  Mephistopheles Tiefling
  •  Rock Gnome
  •  Seldarine Drow
  •  Wood Half-Elf

The races and subraces not covered by hirelings are:

  •  Asmodeus Tiefling
  •  Deep Gnome
  •  Drow Half-Elf
  •  Forest Gnome
  •  Lolth-Sworn Drow (Covered by Minthara companion)
  •  Shield Dwarf
  •  Strongheart Halfling
  •  Wood Elf (Covered by Halsin companion)
  •  Zariel Tiefling (Covered by Karlach companion)
  • All  Dragonborn subraces.

Outsourcing
Recruit a hireling. You can befriend them or use them as cannon-fodder - we won't judge.

Notes

  1. ↑ Although hirelings are traditionally defined as working (in whole or material part) for money, these characters are literally brought back from the dead for the player character's conscription by  Withers. Also, their backstories indicate that they are arguably more motivated by the prospect of avenging themselves (or those close to them) against the Absolute than for money.
  2. ↑ Although their identity is explicitly categorized as male within the character customization menu, Kerz's in-game backstory and descriptions utilize nonbinary pronouns (They/them).
  3. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Kree and Madala use the same voice actor.
  4. ↑ Although refered to as "They", the backstory given for Maddala in-game says "her village" not "their village". "They", used in-game, is likely plural, referring to both Madalla and the other True Soul.

Bugs

  • When a hireling is  Disguised, they cannot be spoken with, and therefore cannot be dismissed to camp until this condition is removed.
  • In what may be an oversight, if a hireling’s appearance is customised during recruitment, their default portrait still appears in the party's dialogue history.
